stage: development only; no test recording or test scene was read
rule: Among the gated candidates (v2 with longer fit windows, and the observer-bank variants), pick the one with the highest median, over development acoustic recordings that have reference tones, of the tone-bin gain averaged over both horizons. Eligible only if, on development material: (a) whole-band boosts (whole 35-350 Hz band below -0.5 dB at either horizon, any development recording) are no more than v2 + gate has; (b) third-octave boosts (a third-octave band 1 dB or more louder, any development recording and horizon) are no more than v2 + gate has; (c) the median whole-band gain over development acoustic recordings, averaged over both horizons, is at least v2 + gate's minus 0.1 dB; (d) the mean synthetic development objective (release-study objective) is at least v2 + gate's minus 0.5 dB and its synthetic windows below -0.5 dB are no more than v2 + gate has; (e) the compute time it adds per 10 ms block, excluding the tone-selector update that v2 also runs, is below 5 ms at the 99th percentile (offline Python, one thread, measured under the parallel pool). AR methods are comparators, not candidates: they give no per-tone output, which tune-by-ear needs. If no candidate is eligible, v2 stays.
labels: Reference-signal prediction only. Not acoustic attenuation.
